report:
Reviewed the complete restrictions_and_gaps claim, its one implementation association and complete one-test set from review start, and captured the containing sage_ir model and review policy using review read. This is acceptance of explicit deferred evidence, not approval of implemented restriction classification.

The claim has four connected obligations: deliberate restrictions define and explain the supported contract; temporary gaps within otherwise supported Rust are attached as TODOs to the relevant specification anchors with limitations and evidence; those temporary gaps must not silently narrow that contract; and RFDs record their closure plans. The sole implementation association is in sage_meta::todo in service_spec.rs and explicitly says uniform restriction/completeness accounting is not enforced at every semantic boundary. The adjacent modeled explicit_restrictions and represented_completeness claims establish the relevant distinction and semantic context; neither supplies implementation evidence for this anchor. The TODO therefore honestly defers the cross-cutting accounting needed to demonstrate the complete claim. The same captured service_spec file contains concrete visible TODO limitations on other specification anchors, but these examples are not a comprehensive inventory or proof of the contract.

The sole associated test, todo::crates_sage_ir_crate_restrictions_and_gaps, has no executable assertions. Its comment describes the missing documentation review: trace every unsupported fixture to a deliberate restriction or a capability gap and roadmap owner, rejecting restrictions justified only by missing implementation. That explicitly deferred audit covers restriction-versus-gap classification, ownership and planning, and prevention of silently narrowing the contract. Completing it requires a comprehensive unsupported-fixture inventory, restriction rationales and supported-capability declarations, mappings to relevant anchor TODOs and limitations/evidence, and RFD closure-plan links. Those inputs and the uniform accounting named by the implementation TODO are prerequisites; a passing empty test would prove none of these properties. In particular, misclassifying an unimplemented supported construct as a deliberate restriction or omitting an RFD closure plan would escape the current placeholder and remains deferred, rather than being accepted as verified behavior.

There are no ordinary implementation entries, ordinary associated tests, N/A entries, or helper calls to assess. All requirements are accounted for by the explicit implementation and test TODOs and their prerequisites, so no routine evidence edits are requested. Source review used cargo meta review start and review read; no behavioral tests or workspace build were run for this documentation-only review, and no test-execution success is claimed.
